intro: Once a year, the plan needs maintenance more than it needs new ideas. This checklist is dated: pick the review year, tick items as you go (progress stays in this browser), and export it as Markdown or print it. Each item carries a suggested month; the 2026 figures shown come from the verified figures layer and are replaced each January (see the maintenance ritual in the repository docs). Educational only, not financial or tax advice.

items.title: Reset contributions to this year's limits
items.body: Indexed limits change every January. For 2026: 401(k)/403(b) employee deferral {{fig:limit_401k_deferral}} (catch-up at 50+ {{fig:limit_401k_catchup_50}}; ages 60–63 {{fig:limit_401k_supercatchup_6063}}), IRA {{fig:limit_ira}} (catch-up {{fig:limit_ira_catchup}}), HSA {{fig:limit_hsa_self}} self-only / {{fig:limit_hsa_family}} family. Raise payroll elections so the deferral is spread across the year; health FSA ({{verify:2026 health FSA salary-reduction limit — IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32}}) and dependent-care FSA ({{verify:2026 §129 limit — P.L. 119-21 §70404; IRS Publication 15-B (2026)}}) elections are made at open enrollment.

items.title: Pull your credit reports and confirm the freezes are on
items.body: Check all three reports at AnnualCreditReport.com for accounts you do not recognize, and confirm a security freeze is in place at each bureau.

items.title: Run a withholding check
items.body: After filing last year's return, run the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator with a current pay stub and file a new W-4 if the projection is far from zero — especially after a raise, a second job, a marriage or a new child.

items.title: Take a net-worth snapshot
items.body: Assets minus liabilities, recorded on the same date each year. The year-over-year change is the only number that measures real progress, and the list itself is the inventory your family would need in an emergency.

items.title: Audit subscriptions and recurring charges
items.body: Go through a few months of statements for recurring charges. Bank fees — overdraft, ATM, monthly maintenance — often cost more than any single subscription and are worth the same scrutiny.

items.title: Check the allocation against its rebalancing bands
items.body: Compare the current mix to your target and rebalance if any asset class has drifted outside its band; use new contributions first to avoid realizing gains.

items.title: Review insurance at open enrollment
items.body: Most employers hold open enrollment in the fall. Re-check health plan choice, disability coverage, term life against current dependents and debts, and whether property, auto and umbrella liability limits still match your net worth.

items.title: Review beneficiary designations and estate documents
items.body: Open every retirement account, life policy and transfer-on-death registration and confirm the named beneficiaries; check that the will, power of attorney and healthcare directive still name the right people.

items.title: Year-end tax moves
items.body: Before December 31: harvest tax losses in taxable accounts if useful, take any required minimum distribution, make planned charitable gifts or qualified charitable distributions, and use the gift annual exclusion ({{fig:gift_annual_exclusion}} per recipient for 2026) if gifting.
